test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 5 Feb 2021 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which out of these is the Harappan site discovered in Gujarat?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Dholavira.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dholavira**

 
 
• Dholavira is one of the two largest Harappan sites in India discovered in Gujarat.
 
• It is locally known as **Kotada** which means large fort.
 
• The excavation found a decline of the civilization in the **5th of 7th stages.**
 
• UNESCO has included Dholavira of Kutch in the list of **World Heritage Sites in 2021.**
 
• It is one of the **five largest Harappan sites.**
 
• It is also considered as having been the grandest of cities of its time.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Manda**

 
 
• Manda is a village and an **archaeological** site in Jammu in the Indian Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir.
 
• It was excavated by the Archaeological Survey of India during **1976-77 by J. P. Joshi.**
 
• The site contains ruins of an ancient Indus Valley civilization.
 
• It is considered the** northmost site** of the Indus Valley civilization.
 
 
 
• **Balathal**
 
 
• Balathal is an archaeological site.
 
• It is located in Vallabhnagar tehsil of Udaipur district of Rajasthan state in western India.
 
• It is one of the ninety** Ahar-Banas culture sites **located in the Basins of the Banas river and its tributaries.
 
• It was excavated from **1994 to 2000.**
